title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
code: library(reslife) #> Loading required package: pracma #> Loading required package: flexsurv #> Loading required package: survival #> Loading required package: gsl #>  #> Attaching package: 'gsl' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:pracma': #>  #>     Ci, erf, erfc, eta, expint_E1, expint_Ei, fact, hypot, psi, Si, #>     sinc, zeta library(flexsurv) library(survival)

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: reslifefsr() function calculates residual life values directly fitted flexsurvreg object. supports baseline (intercept-) models models patient-level covariate profiles via newdata.

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: begin fitting intercept-generalized gamma model (gengamma.orig) breast cancer dataset bc flexsurv. evaluate mean residual life elapsed time 1 year (life = 1). can verify accuracy analytical derivation direct numerical integration survival function: MRL(x)=1S(x)∫x∞S(t)dt\text{MRL}(x) = \frac{1}{S(x)} \int_x^\infty S(t) \, dt analytical formula reslifefsr() matches numerical integration.
code: fs1 <- flexsurvreg(Surv(recyrs, censrec) ~ 1, data = bc, dist = "gengamma.orig") r <- reslifefsr(obj = fs1, life = 1, type = "mean") r #> [1] 7.194108 # Extract parameters on their natural scale from the fitted model b <- as.numeric(fs1$res["shape", "est"]) a <- as.numeric(fs1$res["scale", "est"]) k <- as.numeric(fs1$res["k", "est"])  # Define survival function surv_gengamma <- function(t) {   pgengamma.orig(t, shape = b, scale = a, k = k, lower.tail = FALSE) }  # Numerical integration integral_val <- integrate(surv_gengamma, lower = 1, upper = Inf)$value sx_val <- surv_gengamma(1) mx_integral <- integral_val / sx_val  all.equal(r, mx_integral) #> [1] "Mean relative difference: 1.597394e-08"

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: model includes covariates, reslifefsr() evaluates residual life across patient profiles. illustrate using bc dataset added covariate age: Evaluating residual life across fitted observations returns vector one value per observation: can also inspect median residual life: extract full summary table (mean, median, custom quantile):
code: set.seed(42) newbc <- bc newbc$age <- rnorm(nrow(bc), mean = 65 - scale(newbc$recyrs, scale = FALSE), sd = 5)  fsr2 <- flexsurvreg(Surv(recyrs, censrec) ~ group + age, data = newbc, dist = "weibull") head(reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, type = "mean"), 5) #> [1] 244.6992 head(reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, type = "median"), 5) #> [1] 209.3608 head(reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, p = 0.8, type = "all"), 5) #>       mean   median percentile #> 1 244.6992 209.3608   376.0821

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: can evaluate specific patient profiles passing data.frame newdata: reslifefsr() invariant column order: Extra unmodeled columns safely ignored:
code: newdata <- data.frame(   group = c("Medium", "Good", "Poor"),   age   = c(43, 35, 39) )  reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, p = 0.6, type = "all", newdata = newdata) #>        mean    median percentile #> 1 13.988900 11.528209  14.370289 #> 2 39.695764 33.514429  41.148687 #> 3  9.325262  7.571392   9.512931 # Reordered columns produce identical results newdata_reorder <- data.frame(age = c(43, 35, 39), group = c("Medium", "Good", "Poor")) reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, p = 0.6, type = "all", newdata = newdata_reorder) #>        mean    median percentile #> 1 13.988900 11.528209  14.370289 #> 2 39.695764 33.514429  41.148687 #> 3  9.325262  7.571392   9.512931 newdata_extra <- cbind(newdata, extra = c(100, 100, 100)) reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, p = 0.6, type = "all", newdata = newdata_extra) #>        mean    median percentile #> 1 13.988900 11.528209  14.370289 #> 2 39.695764 33.514429  41.148687 #> 3  9.325262  7.571392   9.512931

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: required covariates missing, reslifefsr() informs user: Similarly, invalid factor level supplied:
code: newdata_missing <- data.frame(group = c("Medium", "Good", "Poor")) reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, type = "all", newdata = newdata_missing) #> Error in `form.model.matrix()`: #> ! Value of covariate "age" not supplied in "newdata" newdata_bad_level <- data.frame(group = c("Medium", "Good", "InvalidLevel"), age = c(43, 35, 39)) reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = 4, type = "all", newdata = newdata_bad_level) #> Error in `model.frame.default()`: #> ! factor group has new levels InvalidLevel

what: Plotting Mean Residual Life over Time
title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: can evaluate residual life changes elapsed time xx specific patient profile:
code: patient1 <- newbc[1, ] time_grid <- 1:10  mrl_vals <- sapply(time_grid, function(t0) {   reslifefsr(obj = fsr2, life = t0, type = "mean", newdata = patient1) })  plot(time_grid, mrl_vals, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue",      xlab = "Elapsed Survival Time (Years)",      ylab = "Mean Residual Life (Years)",      main = "Mean Residual Life Function for Patient Profile") grid()

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: standalone function residlife() computes residual life directly distribution names parameter vectors without requiring flexsurvreg object. Supported distributions include: * "exponential" / "exp" * "weibull" * "gamma" * "gompertz" * "lognormal" / "lnorm" * "llogis" * "gengamma" * "gengamma.orig" * "genf" * "genf.orig"

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: residlife() accepts numeric vector elapsed times:
code: t_seq <- seq(1, 10, by = 1) pars_weibull <- c(shape = 1.272, scale = 6.191)  residlife(values = t_seq, distribution = "weibull", parameters = pars_weibull, type = "mean") #>  [1] 5.280618 4.994025 4.776287 4.599837 4.451537 4.323832 4.211904 4.112464 #>  [9] 4.023161 3.942246

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: Parameter order matter long names match: distributions alternative parameterizations like Gamma (rate vs. scale), residlife() seamlessly converts :
code: # Unordered names work identically residlife(values = 5, distribution = "weibull", parameters = c(scale = 6.191, shape = 1.272)) #> [1] 4.451537 # Parameterized by scale residlife(values = 5, distribution = "gamma", parameters = c(shape = 1.272, scale = 6.191)) #> [1] 6.988622  # Parameterized by rate (rate = 1 / scale) residlife(values = 5, distribution = "gamma", parameters = c(shape = 1.272, rate = 1 / 6.191)) #> [1] 6.988622

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
code: residlife(values = c(1, 3, 5), distribution = "weibull", parameters = pars_weibull, p = 0.75, type = "all") #>       mean   median percentile #> 1 5.280618 4.151524   7.446750 #> 2 4.776287 3.629997   6.759695 #> 3 4.451537 3.314545   6.293929

title: 'reslife' Package Demonstration
text: residlife() natively vectorizes values, generating MRL curve requires manual loops:
code: times <- seq(0.1, 10, by = 0.2) mrl_curve <- residlife(values = times, distribution = "weibull", parameters = pars_weibull, type = "mean")  plot(times, mrl_curve, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "darkred",      xlab = "Elapsed Time (x)",      ylab = "Mean Residual Life e(x)",      main = "Weibull Mean Residual Life Curve") grid()

title: Calculate Mean Residual Life (MRL) and Related Values for Different Distributions
code: library(reslife) library(flexsurv) library(survival)  # 1. Evaluate standalone distribution parameters pars_weibull <- c(shape = 1.27, scale = 6.19) residlife(values = c(1, 3, 5), distribution = "weibull", parameters = pars_weibull, type = "all")  # 2. Evaluate from a fitted flexsurvreg model fit <- flexsurvreg(Surv(recyrs, censrec) ~ group, data = bc, dist = "weibull") reslifefsr(obj = fit, life = 2, type = "all")

title: Calculating Residual Life Values — residlife
text: Calculates residual life values range values. Allows user specify distribution parameters.

title: Calculating Residual Life Values — residlife
code: residlife(values, distribution, parameters, p = 0.5, type = "mean")

title: Calculating Residual Life Values — residlife
text: values Range values residual life calculated.Usually given vector. distribution Name distribution. Needs one 'weibull', 'gompertz', 'gamma', 'gengamma.orig', 'exponential', 'lnorm', 'llogis', 'genf', 'genf.orig'. parameters Parameters survival function. Needs inputted order vector, name parameter included. p Percentile calculate residual life. Default .5. type Type residual life outputted. Must "mean", "median", "percentile", "". Default "mean".

title: Calculate Residual Life Values Using a flexsurvreg() Object — reslifefsr
text: obj fitted flexsurvreg object package flexsurv. life Scalar numeric value elapsed time calculate residual life. p Percentile quantile residual life. Default 0.5. type Type residual life return: "mean", "median", "quantile", "percentile", "". Default "mean". newdata data frame containing covariate values evaluate. Default empty (evaluates baseline).

title: Calculate Residual Life Values Using a flexsurvreg() Object — reslifefsr
code: library(flexsurv) fitg <- flexsurvreg(Surv(futime, fustat) ~ 1, data = ovarian, dist = "gengamma") reslifefsr(obj = fitg, life = 6, p = 0.75, type = "all") #>       mean   median percentile #> 1 913.9498 903.1636   2856.237  fitg2 <- flexsurvreg(Surv(futime, fustat) ~ age, data = ovarian, dist = "gengamma") df_new <- data.frame(age = c(50, 65)) reslifefsr(obj = fitg2, life = 3, type = "median", newdata = df_new) #> [1] 1368.6166  366.1353
